newsitem.title: CHINA: China to tackle unlicensed rural cooperative funds.
newsitem.headline: China to tackle unlicensed rural cooperative funds.

text.p: China will next year crack down unlicensed rural cooperative funds to maintain economic and social order among China's huge rural population, the Xinhua news agency said on Friday.

The rural financing bodies first appeared in the early 1980s when China abandoned its communes and introduced a market-oriented responsiblity system, it quoted Duan Xiaosing, deputy director of the State Council, or cabinet, Inter-Department Coordinative Group for Rural Financial Reforms as saying.

These funds were set up by local town and township governments as non-profitmaking organisations to finance agricultural development, he said. None were granted licences to engage in money-making ventures.
However, due to rapid expansion and ignorance among rural authorities, most have have engaged in banking activities such as handling deposits and loans, he said.

The illegal banking activities have led to a large number of problems with many funds losing money, thus affecting their depositors and resulting in social instability and hampering agricultural growth, Duan said.
The amounts involved were huge, he said, but declined to reveal how many funds existed or how much money was involved.
"Rectification should be implemented without any delay and hesitation," the Xinhua news agency quoted Duan as saying.
Funds will first be registered and then be classified while those that have violated the law will be closed.
"It will be a very tough job," he said.
